t.E239.agn: In 2014 EFSA could not set its own ADI because the data were insufficient; it stated that use at the maximum permitted level in Provolone cheese (25 mg/kg, expressed as formaldehyde) would not raise a safety concern, but that new toxicity data might be needed to extend its uses. In 1973 JECFA had set the ADI at 0–0.15 mg/kg body weight.
t.E239.body: It breaks down into formaldehyde under acidic conditions.
t.E239.eff.0.a: No concern according to EFSA at the permitted level (25 mg/kg)
t.E239.eff.0.t: It breaks down into formaldehyde under acidic conditions; according to IARC, formaldehyde is carcinogenic to humans (Group 1). EFSA saw no safety concern at the permitted level in Provolone cheese
t.E239.eval: A preservative; it breaks down into formaldehyde in an acidic environment. IARC classifies formaldehyde as Group 1 (carcinogenic to humans) (Monograph 100F, 2012). In the EU it is authorised only in Provolone cheese. In 2014 EFSA could not set its own ADI owing to insufficient data; it concluded that use at the maximum permitted level (25 mg/kg, expressed as formaldehyde) does not raise a safety concern.
t.E239.prod: Produced chemically by reacting formaldehyde with ammonia in water.
t.E239.regx.0: Re-evaluated; no ADI could be set, no safety concern for the current use in Provolone.
t.E239.regx.2: Only in ripened Provolone cheese, 25 mg/kg residue expressed as formaldehyde.
t.E239.summary: A preservative made from formaldehyde and ammonia. In the EU it is authorised only in Italian Provolone cheese.
t.E239.what: It is a preservative that prevents microbial spoilage and is authorised in the EU only in Provolone cheese.
